title: In-App Surveys Need Lots of Guardrails
intro: Single-question 1–5 pop-ups are easy to launch and badly overused. Written for complex, lower-frequency enterprise workflows.

topics.title: In-App Surveys Need Lots of Guardrails

learn.title: Five guardrails
learn.text:
**1. Purpose** — task-level, not overall sentiment
**2. Trigger** — on attempts, not only completions
**3. Stop rule** — around 55 per segment; cut off past 100
**4. Exposure** — cooldowns, and one survey per session
**5. Compare** — same workflow, same users, same trigger

Overall sentiment and benchmarking belong in periodic instruments (SUS, SUPR-Q, NPS). Pop-ups measure one task.

try.q: What should an in-app pop-up measure?

learn.title: Completion-only triggers lie
learn.text:
If the survey fires only on success, **you hear only from people who made it**.

The users who abandoned, hit errors or needed help never see the question — and they are the ones whose experience you were trying to measure.

try.q: Your satisfaction score is high but support tickets are rising. What's a likely cause?
options: The survey only fires on completion
The rating scale has too few points to be sensitive
try.explain: Survivors answer; the people who failed never saw it.

learn.title: Write it down before launch
learn.text:
Before it goes live, record: **purpose, audience segment, target sample, other active surveys, and a stop rule.**

Without that, pop-ups accumulate — several running at once, firing indefinitely, with nobody able to say what any of them was for.

*High-traffic consumer products can loosen several of these limits.*

try.q: What is the stop rule for?
options: Ending collection at the target sample
Setting the significance threshold before launch
Choosing when to repeat the survey
try.explain: Around 55 per segment, cut off past 100 — then stop asking.

test.q: Who is this guidance written for?
options: High-traffic consumer apps with frequent repeat visits
test.explain: Consumer products with lots of traffic can loosen the limits.

test.q: What belongs in a periodic instrument rather than a pop-up?
options: Feature-level feedback on a specific screen
test.explain: SUS, SUPR-Q or NPS, run on a schedule.

test.q: How many surveys should a user see in one session?
options: None, if they answered last week

test.q: What makes two in-app survey results comparable?
options: Identical question wording, whatever else changed
test.explain: Change any of the three and you're comparing different things.

test.q: What should be written down before launch?
options: Purpose, segment, target, other surveys, stop rule
The analysis plan, chart templates and reporting schedule
The list of stakeholders to notify
test.explain: It's what stops pop-ups accumulating unmanaged.
